signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Hopes
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades at 112.428 amid a massive G10 performance gap. JPY is the week's clear leader, up 1.538% (n=7), while CAD lags at -0.653% (n=3), creating a 2.191% spread. This JPY outperformance is fundamentally at odds with the carry deficit, as CAD holds a 125bp advantage over JPY. The move is accelerated by a 50-50 chance of a Strait of Hormuz deal and US sanctions relief for Iran, which removes the oil supply risk premium and weighs on CAD while lifting JPY sentiment. JPY ESI at +22.9 confirms a strong positive data surprise trend supporting the bid. Technically, USD/JPY has fallen below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (161.88/161.25/158.0), signaling a major trend shift. Risk: Hormuz deal negotiations collapse, reviving the oil supply risk premium and reversing CAD weakness.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Volatility + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY at 157.62 shows an extreme dislocation between carry and sentiment. While the 275bp Fed-BoJ OIS spread still heavily favors USD, the options market is pricing in aggressive downside protection with a 25d Risk Reversal of -2.40—a strong put skew. CFTC data shows JPY specs remain net short -124,575, leaving the pair vulnerable to a massive short-squeeze as price trades below the SMA200 at 158.0. Negative VRP of -1.1% (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.3%) suggests the options market is underpricing the realized volatility of this move, creating an asymmetric setup for further downside. The JPY real rate of -0.70% remains accommodative, yet the pair continues to ignore carry in favor of safe-haven flows and geopolitical de-escalation. Risk: US 10Y yields spike back above 4.80%, reasserting carry dominance and stalling the JPY recovery.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5881, comfortably above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5814/0.5793/0.5827. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. This data outperformance contradicts the heavy speculative short, creating a high-conviction squeeze setup as price holds above long-term moving averages. Despite a -1.56% negative real rate, the OCR-overnight at 2.50% vs Fed SOFR at 3.65% presents a 115bp carry disadvantage that specs are fading too aggressively. If the RBNZ delivers a hawkish surprise on September 2, the crowded short will be forced to cover into an uptrend. Risk: RBNZ pivots to neutral on September 2, validating the spec short position.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Volatility + Retail Sentiment Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7054 is testing its SMA20/50 cluster at 0.6986/0.7007. Options demand is significantly elevated with an IV of 11.3% against an HV30 of 6.2%, resulting in a +5.0% Vol Risk Premium. Retail sentiment is 75% short, diverging from the COT LF net long of +23,616. This institutional-retail divergence typically supports further upside as retail traders unsuccessfully fade the trend. The 70bp AONIA-SOFR carry advantage in favor of AUD provides structural support, even as AUD ESI shows persistent data misses at -15.5. The market is currently valuing the carry and institutional positioning over the weakening domestic data. Risk: A close below the SMA50 at 0.7007 would invalidate the bullish retail-divergence thesis.
